thread.title: Aaron Bean votes for balanced budget amendment in U.S. House

author: a. i. medina
title: Aaron Bean votes for balanced budget amendment in U.S. House
text:
U.S. Congressman Aaron Bean voted on Mar. 18 in favor of H.J. Res. 139, a proposed amendment to the U.S. Constitution that would require the federal government to maintain a balanced budget and limit deficit spending.
The vote reflects ongoing debates about federal fiscal responsibility and efforts to address government spending practices. The measure aimed to introduce stricter controls on how much the federal government can spend each year.
After casting his vote, Bean said, “If hardworking families are required to live within their means, then the federal government should do the same. But in Crazy Town, the instinct is always to spend more of the taxpayers’ money. That’s why I voted in favor of the balanced budget amendment modeled after states like Florida. It puts real guardrails in place to stop Crazy Town from prioritizing short-term spending over America’s long-term future.”
H.J. Res. 139 would have limited federal expenditures to an average based on annual revenue collected over the previous three years, with adjustments for inflation and population growth. The proposal included an exception for times of national emergency or war, which would require approval by a two-thirds supermajority in both chambers of Congress.
Bean is currently serving in Congress representing Florida’s 4th district after replacing John Rutherford in 2023, according to official records. He has served as a member of Congress since 2023 and previously held positions in both the Florida House of Representatives from 2000 to 2008 and the Florida Senate from 2012 to 2022, as reported by the Florida House. Bean was born in Fernandina Beach, Florida in 1967 and continues to reside there at age 56, according to Ballotpedia. He graduated from Jacksonville University with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1989.
Despite support from Bean and others, H.J. Res. 139 did not pass, failing by a vote of 211-207.
